subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Enron's House of Cards
description: One-minute skill: Enron's House of Cards.

hook.text: Enron was named America's most innovative company six years running — while hiding billions in debt.

buildup.text: Executives used off-balance-sheet entities to hide losses and inflate profits for years.

discovery.text: Enron's stock went from $90 to $0.26 once the accounting fraud was exposed.

twist.text: Arthur Andersen, one of the Big Five accounting firms, shredded documents and collapsed too.

climax.text: Twenty thousand employees lost jobs and retirement savings. Top executives went to prison.

punchline.text: Innovation awards don't detect hidden debt.

quiz.question: What happened to Arthur Andersen after Enron?
options: It was acquired by a rival
